results.title: We tell you when we cancel a price increase - Autoresearch - Autoresearch
highlights:
01:00 UTC

### We tell you when we cancel a price increase

You say to your agent

> “Is the H100 price increase that you announced still on?”

If we cancel a price increase that we announced, the dashboard shows a notice that says so. Each organization that got the email about the increase gets a second email that cancels it. The email includes the text of the first one. See Rates.

## October 14, 2026

1. 23:00 UTC

### Sandbox price increases come with notice too

You say to your agent

> “Will sandbox prices go up while my rollouts run?”

A sandbox rate increase now also comes at least 24 hours before it takes effect, and we tell you about it. That is any higher rate: active sandboxes, parked sandboxes and snapshots, or cold snapshots.

The dashboard shows a notice until a few days after the increase takes effect. The admins and billing members of each organization that used sandboxes in the last 90 days get an email. A new rate applies to each billing hour that starts at or after that time. See Rates.

...

## October 13, 2026

1. 20:00 UTC

### We tell you about a price increase before it takes effect

You say to your agent

> “Is the price of an H100 going to change soon?”

A price increase now always comes at least 24 hours before it takes effect, and we tell you about it. An increase is a higher list price, or a smaller Friday, weekend, or batch job discount.

When we schedule an increase, the dashboard shows a notice until a few days after it takes effect. The admins and billing members of each organization that used that type in the last 90 days get an email.

Your agent sees it too. Until the increase takes effect, `create_node` and `get_node` carry it in `rate.upcoming_increase`, and `submit_job` carries it in `upcoming_increase`. The field gives the time it takes effect, the new list rate per GPU and per node, and the new discounts. A running node also gets a `price_change` event on `/v1/events`. See Rates.

...

## October 8, 2026

1. 07:00 UTC

### The H100 price is now $5.04 per GPU-hour

On October 8 at 00:00 Pacific time, the H100 list price changed from $3.96 to $5.04 per GPU-hour. Per GPU-minute, the price changed from $0.066 to $0.084. A whole 8-GPU node now costs $40.32 per hour.

The new price applies to each minute that we bill from that time. This includes the minutes of nodes and jobs that were already running. Minutes before that time bill at the old price.

The discounts did not change, and they now apply to the new list price. Friday hours are 33% off, and Saturday and Sunday hours are 20% off, on the Pacific calendar. Batch jobs are 25% off the list price. The docs show the rates.

We did not tell you about this change before it took effect. We are sorry for the late notice. If you have a question about your bill, send it to us on the contact page.

...

### There is no minimum charge

The pricing table and the docs called the idle window a “per-session minimum”. It never was one. A node that goes idle keeps running for its idle window, and it bills while it runs. If you stop the node, billing ends at the stop. A session that ran two minutes pays two minutes.

You say to your agent

> “Stop the node as soon as the run finishes.”

The pricing table now reads “15 min idle window ($0.90 at most)” on a 1x node, and the docs say the same. Nothing about billing changed. `rate.minimum_minutes` and `rate.session_minimum_usd` keep their names in the API. They report the length of the idle window and what the whole window costs if you let it run out. See the docs.
3.

...

Billed seconds are the seconds for one GPU. The charge is seconds x `gpu_count` x rate / 60.

...

Nothing else moved. Every call, parameter, and id is unchanged, the rates are the same, and the docs section keeps its address. Three labels read differently. The two pricing rows are now Sandboxes (active) and Sandboxes (parked), and the line on your usage page and your invoice is Sandboxes. If a script of yours matches on those strings, that is the one thing to update.

results.title: Introducing InfiniBand clusters in SF Autoresearch | SF Compute
results.author: San Francisco Compute
highlights:
Introducing InfiniBand clusters in SF Autoresearch | SF Compute

# Introducing InfiniBand clusters in SF Autoresearch#

October 3, 2026

InfiniBand clusters in SF Autoresearch

San Francisco Compute

We’re introducing InfiniBand clusters in SF Autoresearch. Create a group of dedicated H100 machines, connect them over a private InfiniBand network, and run distributed training from your terminal or agent.

Clusters extend Autoresearch to experiments that need GPUs on several machines working together. Each node contributes eight H100 GPUs. InfiniBand RDMA provides the connection between machines for NCCL operations such as exchanging gradients during training.

Each cluster gets a fresh Elastic InfiniBand Partition. Autoresearch places the nodes on the same fabric and manages their partition membership. You use the same commands to run code, copy files, and read logs that you use on an individual node.

Clusters are currently in internal preview. Contact us to register your interest in customer access.

...

## Pay for the minutes you run#

Each member bills at the ordinary eight-GPU node rate from the moment it is ready, with no minimum charge. You do not pay while the cluster waits for capacity or prepares its machines. Deleting the cluster stops billing without waiting for the machines to leave the partition.

Our 38-minute validation run cost about $27 at that test’s Friday-discounted rate of $0.71 per minute for both nodes.
